summary: Create a Google Cloud project, configure the OAuth consent screen, choose the minimum Gmail scopes, and create an OAuth client with a valid redirect URI. The main catch is that most useful Gmail scopes are sensitive or restricted, so external production apps need verification and some restricted scopes also require a security assessment. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/web-server))
difficultyReason: Gmail setup is self-serve, but production access is not trivial because sensitive/restricted scopes trigger Google verification, and restricted scopes can require a security assessment. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/13463073?hl=en))

timeToFirstLogin.text: Same day to a few hours in testing, once the project, client, and test user are in place. (Estimate)

timeToProduction.text: A few days to several weeks if Google requires brand verification or restricted-scope review; longer if a security assessment is needed. (Estimate)

costs.text: Standard Gmail API use has no direct Google API fee.
costs.quote: All standard use of the Gmail API is available at no additional cost.

costs.text: If you exceed quota request limits later in 2026, Google says charges will be added to your Google Cloud bill; quota increase requests will also require Google Cloud billing to be enabled.
costs.quote: API usage over standard daily thresholds will generate charges on your Google Cloud bill.

costs.text: If you need a restricted-scope security assessment, the third-party assessor fee is not published by Google and will depend on the assessor.

requirements.text: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API.
requirements.quote: creating a project in the Google API Console and enabling the API.

requirements.text: Configure the OAuth consent screen with app name, support email, and contact email.
requirements.quote: All apps using OAuth 2.0 require a consent screen configuration

requirements.text: Verify your authorized domains, and keep your homepage and privacy policy on the same verified domain.
requirements.quote: Google requires verification of all domains

requirements.text: Choose External for public users or Internal for a Google Workspace organization.
requirements.quote: available to any user with a Google Account.

requirements.text: Add only the minimum Gmail scopes you need.
requirements.quote: choose the most narrowly focused scope possible

requirements.text: Register the OAuth redirect URI exactly as Google expects it, including scheme, host, and path.
requirements.quote: must exactly match one of the authorized redirect URIs

requirements.text: Request offline access so you receive a refresh token and can keep the connection alive.
requirements.quote: it also receives a refresh token

reviewTriggers.text: Any external production app that requests sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes must complete Google OAuth app verification.
reviewTriggers.quote: Apps that request access to scopes categorized as sensitive or restricted must complete Google's OAuth app verification before being granted access.

reviewTriggers.text: If you want your app name or logo shown on the consent screen, you need brand verification.
reviewTriggers.quote: you will need to complete a lighter-weight verification process known as brand-verification.

reviewTriggers.text: If the app accesses restricted Gmail data from or through a third-party server, Google requires an annual security assessment.

steps.title: Create the Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Open Google Cloud Console, create a project, and enable Gmail API.
steps.quote: creating a project in the Google API Console and enabling the API.

steps.title: Set up OAuth branding
steps.detail: Go to Google Auth Platform > Branding and fill in the app name, support email, and contact email.
steps.quote: In User support email, choose a support email address

steps.title: Verify your domains
steps.detail: Add your authorized domains and verify ownership in Google Search Console.
steps.quote: Google requires verification of all domains

steps.title: Choose audience and test users
steps.detail: Set Audience to External or Internal. If External, add test users for development.
steps.quote: available to any user with a Google Account.

steps.title: Add Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Go to Data Access and add only the Gmail scopes your agent truly needs.
steps.quote: choose the most narrowly focused scope possible

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Go to Clients, create an OAuth client ID for a Web application, and register the exact redirect URI.
steps.quote: must exactly match one of the authorized redirect URIs

steps.title: Implement offline access
steps.detail: Request offline access, exchange the code, and store the refresh token securely.
steps.quote: it also receives a refresh token

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.detail: If you use sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes, submit verification and wait for Google review.
steps.quote: must complete Google's OAuth app verification before being granted access.

blockers.problem: Testing mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days.
blockers.whatToDo: Use test users for development, but publish before production.
blockers.quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent.

blockers.problem: A redirect URI mismatch will break login.
blockers.whatToDo: Copy the redirect URI exactly from your Composio auth config and register it verbatim in Google Cloud.
blockers.quote: must exactly match one of the authorized redirect URIs

blockers.problem: Restricted Gmail scopes that touch data through your server need a security assessment.
blockers.whatToDo: Plan time and budget for a Google-empanelled assessor before launch.
blockers.quote: must go through a security assessment

agentDrafts.title: App description
agentDrafts.text: Our app is an AI assistant that connects to a user's Gmail account with explicit consent. It reads user-selected email content, drafts replies, and sends messages only when the user approves.

agentDrafts.title: Why we need gmail.send
agentDrafts.text: We need gmail.send so the assistant can send user-approved replies, follow-ups, and notifications from the user's Gmail account.

agentDrafts.title: Why we need gmail.readonly
agentDrafts.text: We need gmail.readonly so the assistant can inspect inbox threads, message content, and headers to summarize mail and draft accurate responses.

agentDrafts.title: Why we need gmail.modify
agentDrafts.text: We need gmail.modify so the assistant can apply user-requested actions like archiving, labeling, or moving messages after the user confirms them.

openQuestions: Do you need send-only access, or do you also need to read inbox content?
Will Gmail data be processed or stored on your server, which would make restricted-scope review and a security assessment more likely?
Is this an external public app, or only an internal Google Workspace app?
